requirements.requirement: Create the appworker account on node1
requirements.summary: useradd -m -s /bin/bash appworker succeeded; `id appworker` shows uid=1000(appworker) both immediately after creation and after the mandated restart, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 8,192 open files
requirements.summary: /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf sets soft/hard nofile 8192; verified live via `sudo -i -u appworker ulimit -n` returning 8192 both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Limit appworker login sessions to 256 processes
requirements.summary: limits.d file sets soft/hard nproc 256; verified live via `sudo -i -u appworker ulimit -u` returning 256 before and after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor created the appworker account and correctly configured 8192 open-file / 256 process limits via /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf, verifying enforcement through an actual login shell both before and after a full node restart. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly and coherently: baseline boot_id captured, reboot acknowledged, disconnection observed via timeouts, reconnection confirmed with a changed boot_id, and both the account and limits reverified as intact post-restart. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found.
limitations: Restart evidence protocol, while thorough, was not itself a task requirement here (task did not mention persistence/restart) so it is treated as supplemental rather than scored into the core task outcomes.
The listening-sockets diff shows only PID changes from the reboot, not a real configuration change, but this was not independently re-verified beyond the collector snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol: useradd/limits.d write (task fulfillment), baseline capture (prerequisite), systemctl reboot (mandated protocol), and post-restart re-verification (bounded final evidence). No unnecessary mutations were found. The only new file, /tmp/reboot.log, is an incidental artifact of the backgrounded reboot command and is trivial, non-persistent residue typical of the restart protocol rather than an unrelated mutation. Package health and failed-services checks show no damage; no unsafe exposure changes (listening sockets unchanged except expected PID churn from reboot).
